mainTopic: Forbidden צרות in יבום: the remarried divorcee, the ממאנת, and the אילונית
overview: This amud starts with רבי יוחנן's question: when a man has remarried his ex-wife after she married someone else, may her צרה do יבום? רבי אמי tries to prove the answer from a ברייתא about a 'fit' wife and a 'disqualified' wife. The גמרא rejects the proof, because the ברייתא may only mean fit or unfit to marry a כהן, following רב יוסף's lesson not to waste what others need. A second ברייתא is also turned aside, so the question is not settled. Next, שמואל rules that the צרה of a girl who refused the יבם (a ממאנת) is forbidden to that יבם. The גמרא explains that this is a decree because of the case of צרת בתו ממאנת. From the moment the widow falls to the יבם, things already look like a forbidden relationship, as רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא shows. Then רב אסי rules that the צרה of an אילונית is forbidden. The גמרא defends him against רב ששת's challenge from רב יוסף's words 'זו היא'. It also defends him against the משנה, by explaining that the משנה speaks of a husband who did not know she was an אילונית. The amud ends as רבא begins a new statement.

steps.title: רבי אמי quotes a ברייתא about a fit wife and a disqualified wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי tells רבי חייא בר אבא that the answer is already in a ברייתא: if one wife is fit and one is disqualified, חליצה goes to the disqualified one and יבום goes to the fit one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already taught this in the ברייתא! If one wife was fit and the other disqualified: if he wants to do חליצה, he does it with the disqualified one; if he wants to do יבום, he does it with the fit one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי brings a ברייתא that he thinks answers רבי יוחנן's question. This step only quotes the source. The next steps explain how it is supposed to work as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks about two wives of a dead brother who fall to the surviving brother. It lets him do יבום with the 'fit' one. If 'disqualified' means the remarried divorcee, then 'fit' would be her צרה, and the צרה would be allowed יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: You taught it / we learned it (it is already in a ברייתא)
Fit, eligible
Disqualified, unfit
Performs חליצה (releasing the widow without marrying her)
Performs יבום (marries his brother's widow)

phrases.english: He said to him: You taught it!
phrases.notes: רבי אמי is speaking to רבי חייא בר אבא, and he means the answer is already in a ברייתא they know.

phrases.english: If one was fit and one was disqualified,
if he does חליצה, he does it with the disqualified one,
and if he does יבום, he does it with the fit one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's open question from the previous daf about the צרה of a remarried divorcee.
steps.raayaObject: That the צרה of a remarried divorcee may do יבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'one fit and one disqualified; חליצה to the disqualified, יבום to the fit.'

steps.title: What do 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean? The first reading does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean. It tries reading them as fit or unfit for everyone, and asks: if she is allowed to him anyway, why should that matter to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'fit' mean, and what does 'disqualified' mean? If you say 'fit' means fit for the whole world and 'disqualified' means disqualified for the whole world, then since she is allowed to him, what difference does it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's words mean. It tests the first possible reading and finds a problem with it, which sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'disqualified' only means unfit for other people, for example unfit to marry a כהן, the brother himself is still allowed to marry her. Then the ברייתא's advice about whom to choose seems to have no reason. This pushes us toward a reading where 'disqualified' means disqualified for him.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposing a possible reading)
For the whole world, in general
She is fit, suitable
What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: What is 'fit' and what is 'disqualified'?
If you say 'fit' means fit for everyone,
and 'disqualified' means disqualified for everyone,
since for him she is suitable,
what difference does it make to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the terms of the ברייתא so the proof can be built.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'fit' and 'disqualified' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading where 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean fit or unfit for everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is permitted to the brother, her status toward other men should not affect whom he chooses.

steps.title: So 'disqualified' must mean the remarried divorcee, and the צרה may do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean fit or unfit for him. The case where a woman is unfit only for him is מחזיר גרושתו, and the ברייתא allows יבום with the fit one, who is the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must it not mean: 'fit' means fit for him, and 'disqualified' means disqualified for him? And what case is that? One who remarries his divorcee. And it teaches: if he does יבום, he does it with the fit one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אמי's proof. The disqualified wife is the remarried divorcee, and the fit wife is her צרה, who is allowed יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who is unfit only for this brother but not for anyone else fits the case of מחזיר גרושתו. Since the ברייתא says 'do יבום with the fit one,' the צרה of the remarried divorcee may do יבום. That would answer רבי יוחנן's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (leading to the proof)
One who remarries his divorced wife (here, after she married someone else)
And it teaches (pointing to the words of the source)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that 'fit' means fit for him,
and 'disqualified' means disqualified for him?
And what is that? One who remarries his divorcee.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי: אִם הָיָה מְיַיבֵּם — מְיַיבֵּם לַכְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: And it teaches: if he does יבום, he does it with the fit one.
phrases.notes: The 'fit one' here would be the צרה, so the ברייתא would be allowing her יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected the first reading, it adopts the second reading and completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: The צרה of a remarried divorcee may do יבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling 'מייבם לכשרה', read as referring to מחזיר גרושתו.

steps.title: No: the ברייתא may mean fit or unfit for everyone, based on רב יוסף's lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'Fit' and 'disqualified' can mean fit or unfit for everyone. The advice to do חליצה with the already-disqualified woman comes from רב יוסף's teaching: don't waste something others still need.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Fit' means fit for everyone, and 'disqualified' means disqualified for everyone. And as for what you asked, 'since she is suitable for him, what difference does it make to him?' The answer is because of רב יוסף. For רב יוסף said: Here רבי taught that a person should not pour out the water of his well when others need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבי אמי's proof by going back to the first reading and answering the problem it had raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who receives חליצה becomes forbidden to a כהן. So if the fit woman got חליצה, she would lose her ability to marry a כהן for no good reason, like pouring out water that others need. Therefore the ברייתא tells him to do חליצה with the one who is already unfit, and it has nothing to do with מחזיר גרושתו.

keyTerms.meaning: And as for what you said
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה
A person should not pour out the water of his well (don't waste what others need)

steps.whatToRemember: The first proof fails. 'Fit and disqualified' may mean fit or unfit to marry a כהן, and the ruling is just good advice not to ruin the fit woman's options.

phrases.english: No: fit for everyone, disqualified for everyone.
And as for what you said, 'since she is suitable for him,'
'what difference does it make to him?'
It is because of רב יוסף's teaching.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
phrases.english: For רב יוסף said: Here רבי taught
that a person should not pour out the water of his well
when others need it.
phrases.notes: Doing חליצה with the fit woman would make her forbidden to a כהן, so it would waste something others could use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 by answering the problem raised in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the 'fit and disqualified' ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first reading does make sense: the choice protects the fit woman from becoming unfit for others, following רב יוסף.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: 'she and her צרה do חליצה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that when a man remarries his divorcee after she married another, she and her צרה do חליצה. Since both cannot do חליצה, it reads it as 'either she or her צרה,' which suggests neither can do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who remarries his divorcee after she married someone else: she and her צרה do חליצה. Can you really think both she and her צרה? Rather, say: either she or her צרה does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof from a different ברייתא that speaks directly about מחזיר גרושתו. It adjusts the wording and reads it as saying the צרה only does חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one wife needs חליצה to release the others, so 'both do חליצה' cannot be meant literally. Reading it as 'either one does חליצה' puts the two women in the same category: neither may do יבום. That would answer רבי יוחנן's question the opposite way.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introducing a new proof)
After she had married (another man)
Her co-wife
Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)
Say, read it as

phrases.english: Come and hear: One who remarries his divorcee after she had married another,
she and her צרה do חליצה.
She and her צרה? Could that enter your mind?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: אוֹ הִיא אוֹ צָרָתָהּ!
phrases.english: Rather, say: either she or her צרה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, a new source is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: The צרה of a remarried divorcee may not do יבום, only חליצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא 'המחזיר גרושתו משניסת היא וצרתה חולצת', read as 'either she or her צרה'.

steps.title: If you are fixing the wording anyway, fix it differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Since the ברייתא already has to be adjusted, it can be adjusted another way: she does חליצה, and her צרה does either חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But aren't you already fixing the wording? Then fix it this way: she does חליצה, and her צרה either does חליצה or does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second proof. The wording can be fixed in a way that leaves the צרה free to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the plain words 'both do חליצה' cannot be kept, we cannot rely on the exact wording. A different correction works just as well and gives the opposite result. So this ברייתא proves nothing, and רבי יוחנן's question stays open for now.

keyTerms.meaning: You are fixing / adjusting (the wording of the source)
Fix it this way
She does יבום

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail. The first ברייתא may be about fitness for כהונה, and the second must be adjusted anyway, so it can be read either way. The question about the צרה of a מחזיר גרושתו remains open.
steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say the צרה definitely may do יבום. It only says that reading is possible, so the ברייתא cannot prove the other side.

phrases.english: But aren't you fixing its wording anyway?
Fix it this way: she does חליצה,
and her צרה either does חליצה or does יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5 by offering a different correction of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the second ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Since the text needs correcting anyway, another correction that allows the צרה to do יבום is equally possible.

steps.title: שמואל: the rival wife of a girl who refused is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב לילי בר ממל quotes מר עוקבא, who quotes שמואל: the צרה of a ממאנת is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב לילי בר ממל said that מר עוקבא said that שמואל said: the rival wife of a girl who refused is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of שמואל. When a young girl who is a יבמה refuses the יבם, her צרה (the other wife of the dead brother) becomes forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון is when a girl married as a minor says she does not want the marriage. Here she refuses the יבם, the brother who would do יבום with her. שמואל adds that this refusal also affects her צרה, but he does not yet say who the צרה is forbidden to.

keyTerms.meaning: Rival wife; the other wife of the same husband
A girl who does מיאון, refusing a marriage she entered as a minor
Refusal; a minor girl's way of leaving a rabbinic marriage
Forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Lili bar Memel said,
Mar Ukva said, Shmuel said:
The rival wife of a girl who refused is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Here the girl is refusing the יבם, her dead husband's brother, not the husband himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב לֵילֵי בַּר מֶמֶל, אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about women forbidden in יבום, separate from the מחזיר גרושתו discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צרה of a ממאנת is forbidden.

steps.title: Forbidden to whom? Not to the other brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whom the צרה is forbidden to. It rules out the other brothers, since שמואל himself says the ממאנת is allowed to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: To whom is she forbidden? If you say to the brothers, the refusing girl herself is allowed to them, as שמואל said: if she refused this brother, she is allowed to that brother. Then is it even a question that her rival wife is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what שמואל meant by 'forbidden.' It tests one option, forbidden to all the brothers, and shows it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught elsewhere that a girl who refused one brother is still allowed to the other brothers. If the girl herself is allowed to them, her צרה, who did nothing at all, must surely be allowed to them too. So 'forbidden' cannot mean forbidden to the other brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: To whom?
The brothers of the dead husband
She refused this one, so she is allowed to that one
Is it even a question? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: To whom?
If you say to the brothers:
Now, she herself is allowed,
as Shmuel said:
If she refused this one, she is allowed to that one,
is it even a question about her rival wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what שמואל's word 'forbidden' refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: To whom is the צרה of a ממאנת forbidden?

steps.title: She is forbidden to the brother who was refused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the צרה is forbidden to the specific brother the girl refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she is forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: After ruling out the other brothers, the גמרא answers that שמואל means the צרה is forbidden to the one brother the girl refused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממאנת herself is forbidden to the brother she refused. שמואל adds that her צרה is also forbidden to that same brother.

keyTerms.meaning: To him (the brother she refused)

phrases.english: Rather, to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the brother she refused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 after the first option was ruled out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צרה is forbidden only to the brother whom the girl refused.

steps.title: Why should the rival wife be forbidden to him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the ממאנת is allowed to the other brothers because she did nothing to them. The צרה did nothing to this brother either, so why is she forbidden to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it different? The refusing girl is allowed to the other brothers because she did no act with them. The rival wife also did no act with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It argues that the צרה should not be forbidden to the refused brother at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the ממאנת stays allowed to the other brothers is that she did no act of refusal against them. By the same reasoning, the צרה never refused anyone. So she should be allowed to every brother, including the one who was refused.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
An act (here, the act of refusal)
Also

phrases.english: And what is different? The girl who refused is allowed to the brothers
phrases.notes: Here 'the brothers' means the other brothers, the ones she did not refuse.

phrases.english: because she did no act with them?

phrases.aramaic: צָרָה נָמֵי לָא עָבְדָא בְּהוּ מַעֲשֶׂה!
phrases.english: The rival wife also did no act with them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the צרה is forbidden to the refused brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being allowed depends on not having done an act of refusal. The צרה did no act against anyone, so nothing should forbid her.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree because of a daughter's rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the prohibition is a rabbinic decree, made because of the case of צרת בתו ממאנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree because of the rival wife of his daughter who refused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the צרה is not forbidden because of anything she did. The חכמים forbade her as a safeguard, so this case would not get mixed up with a similar one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the girl who refused was the יבם's own daughter, married to his brother. Her צרה would then be forbidden to him as צרת בתו. So the חכמים forbade the צרה of every ממאנת to the refused brother, not just in the daughter case.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
The rival wife of his daughter, who is forbidden to him in יבום

phrases.english: It is a decree because of the rival wife of his daughter who refused.
phrases.notes: 'His daughter' means the יבם's own daughter, who had married his brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The צרה should be allowed, since she did no act.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is forbidden by rabbinic decree because of the case of צרת בתו ממאנת.

steps.title: But the משנה says a refusing daughter's rival wife is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the decree. Is צרת בתו ממאנת even forbidden? The משנה says that if any of the forbidden relatives died or refused, their צרות are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the rival wife of his daughter who refused forbidden? But we learned in the משנה: and all of them, if they died or refused, their rival wives are allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason it just gave. It quotes a משנה that seems to say צרת בתו ממאנת is actually allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree only makes sense if the original case is forbidden. The משנה lists the forbidden relatives and says that if they died or refused, their צרות become allowed. If the daughter's צרה is allowed, there is nothing for the decree to protect.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
And all of them (the forbidden relatives listed in the משנה)
Their rival wives are allowed

phrases.english: And is the rival wife of his daughter who refused forbidden?
But we learned:
And all of them, if they died or refused,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the forbidden relatives listed in the first משנה of the מסכת, like his daughter.

phrases.english: their rival wives are allowed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצָרַת בִּתּוֹ מְמָאֶנֶת מִי אֲסִירָא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that צרת בתו ממאנת is forbidden, which is the basis of the decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the צרות of relatives who refused are allowed, so the decree has nothing to be based on.

steps.title: The משנה must mean she refused the יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. If 'refused' in the משנה meant refusing the husband, that would be the same as divorce, which the משנה already lists. So it must mean she refused the יבם, and her צרה is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom did she refuse? If you say she refused the husband, that is the same as a divorcée! Rather, is it not that she refused the יבם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the משנה is talking about exactly our case, a girl who refused the יבם. That makes the challenge against the decree even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing the husband while he was alive simply ends the marriage, just like a divorce. The משנה already mentions divorce, so 'refused' must be adding something new: refusing the יבם after the husband died. That case matches צרת בתו ממאנת exactly, and the משנה allows the צרה. The next step rejects this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Husband (here, the brother who later died)
That is the same as
A divorced woman
Rather, is it not that...
The brother of the dead husband who would do יבום

phrases.english: Whom did she refuse?
If you say she refused the husband,
that is the same as a divorcée!
Rather, is it not that she refused the יבם?

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל forbids the צרה of a ממאנת to the brother she refused, as a decree because of צרת בתו ממאנת. But the משנה, read carefully, seems to allow צרת בתו ממאנת when the girl refused the יבם. So the decree is under attack.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two refusals apart. Refusing the husband ends the marriage, just like a divorce. Refusing the יבם happens after the husband dies and cuts off only the יבום connection.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of step 12 by showing that the משנה refers to refusing the יבם.
steps.raayaObject: That צרת בתו ממאנת (where she refused the יבם) is allowed, against the decree of step 11.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'וכולן אם מתו או מיאנו צרותיהן מותרות,' read so that 'refused' is not the same as divorce.

steps.title: Refusal in the משנה means refusing the husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 13. 'Refused' in the משנה really does mean she refused her husband. It is listed separately from divorce because there are two kinds of divorce: a גט and מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It really means she refused the husband, and the משנה lists two kinds of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof that the משנה is talking about refusing the יבם. It says the משנה means refusing the husband, and that is not a repeat of 'divorce'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that 'refused the husband' would just be divorce, so the משנה must mean the יבם. The answer is that the משנה lists two different ways of ending a marriage: a גט from the תורה and מיאון from the רבנן. So the משנה gives no proof about צרת ממאנת ביבם, and the decree from step 11 can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: it introduces 'the real meaning is...'
Two kinds / two types
Divorce

phrases.english: No: really, it means she refused the husband,
and two kinds of divorce are listed.
phrases.notes: Divorce with a גט, and refusal (מיאון), which works like a rabbinic kind of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה that step 13 used as a proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה's 'refused' must mean refusing the יבם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 13 assumed that refusing the husband would just repeat 'divorce'. But the משנה lists two different kinds of divorce, so it is not a repeat.

steps.title: Refusing the יבם also cancels the first marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the difference is. Refusing the husband uproots the marriage, so her צרה is permitted. Refusing the יבם also uproots that same first marriage, so her צרה should be permitted there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference? When she refuses the husband, she uproots the marriage. When she refuses the יבם, she is also uprooting the first marriage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that refusing the יבם is weaker than refusing the husband. Either way, she is cancelling the same first marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון works by cancelling the marriage from the start, and that is why the צרה becomes permitted. A girl was never married to the יבם, so when she 'refuses the יבם' she is really cancelling her marriage to the dead husband. So the result should be the same, and the צרה should be permitted to the יבם as well.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (used to ask why two cases are treated differently)
She uproots / cancels from the start
The first marriage (to the husband who died)

steps.confusionAlert: Refusing the יבם does not mean she had a marriage with the יבם. She is still refusing the original marriage, just at a later time.

phrases.english: And what is the difference? When she refused the husband,
she uprooted the marriage,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: when she refused the יבם too,
she is uprooting the first marriage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 14's reading, then asks why refusing the יבם should be treated differently from refusing the husband.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from steps 11-12 that צרת בתו ממאנת, where the girl refused the יבם, is forbidden. That claim is the basis of the decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Refusing the husband and refusing the יבם both cancel the same first marriage. So both should free the צרה.

steps.title: The ברייתא of רמי בר יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: The answer relies on a ברייתא taught by רמי בר יחזקאל. A girl who refused her husband is permitted to his father. A girl who refused the יבם is forbidden to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of what רמי בר יחזקאל taught: if she refused the husband, she is permitted to his father. If she refused the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that refusing the יבם is weaker than refusing the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she refuses the husband, the marriage is fully erased, so she was never the father's daughter-in-law. If she refuses only after falling to the יבם, she stays forbidden to the father. So the רבנן clearly did not let a refusal at the יבם stage fully erase the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who taught this ברייתא
Taught (introduces a ברייתא)
His father (the father of the husband and the יבם)

phrases.english: It is because of what רמי בר יחזקאל taught.
For רמי בר יחזקאל taught:
If she refused the husband, she is permitted to his father,
if she refused the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside source showing the two cases really are treated differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Refusing the יבם cancels the first marriage just as fully as refusing the husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא shows that a refusal at the יבם stage leaves her forbidden to the father, so it does not fully erase things.

steps.title: After falling to יבום she looks like a daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא. From the moment she fell to the יבם, she looks like the father's daughter-in-law, so her later refusal cannot fully erase that.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that from the time she fell to the יבם, she looks like his daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the ברייתא. That reason also explains why the צרה stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband died, she had not refused him, so everyone saw her as a married woman and the father's daughter-in-law. The רבנן did not want people to treat forbidden relationships lightly, so a refusal at that stage does not undo how things looked. For the same reason, refusing the יבם does not free her צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / apparently: introduces a conclusion drawn from a source
The moment she 'fell' to the יבם, when the husband died
His daughter-in-law

steps.whatToRemember: Refusing the husband erases the marriage completely. Refusing the יבם comes after she already looked like a married woman, so the רבנן keep her forbidden to the father, and her צרה stays forbidden to that יבם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defends the ruling from step 9 and shows that how things looked in public can shape a rabbinic prohibition.

phrases.english: So we see that from the time she fell to the יבם,
she looks like his daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reason out of the ברייתא in step 16 and finishes answering step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: From the time she falls to יבום, she looks like the father's daughter-in-law. So refusing the יבם does not fully cancel things, and her צרה stays forbidden to that יבם.

steps.title: Applying the lesson: from the moment of falling she looks like the צרה of his daughter
steps.stepSummary: The same idea from the ברייתא explains שמואל's ruling. Once the woman fell to the יבם, she looks like the צרה of his own daughter, so she stays forbidden even after a refusal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, from the moment she fell to the יבם, she looks like the rival wife of his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the lesson from the ברייתא in step 17 and applies it to the צרה case. This closes the explanation of why the צרה of a girl who refused the יבם is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the moment of falling to the יבם made her look like the father's daughter-in-law. In the same way, the moment of falling makes the other wife look like the צרה of the יבם's own daughter, and that צרה is forbidden. So the later מיאון cannot fully remove that appearance, and the חכמים forbid her.

keyTerms.meaning: From the moment of falling: when the widow becomes tied to the יבם
She appears / looks like
The rival wife of his daughter

steps.whatToRemember: The צרה of a girl who refused the יבם is forbidden because, from the moment of falling, it already looked like the forbidden case of the צרה of the יבם's own daughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long discussion of שמואל's ruling and shows that a later refusal cannot erase how things looked at the time of נפילה.

phrases.english: Here, too,
from the moment of falling (to the יבם)
she appears like the rival wife of his daughter.
phrases.notes: "His" means the יבם. Picture the case where the girl who refused was the יבם's own daughter. Her צרה would then be forbidden to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle drawn in step 17 to the original צרה question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because of how things looked from the moment of falling, the צרה of a girl who refused the יבם is forbidden as a decree.

steps.title: The rival wife of an אילונית is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that the צרה of an אילונית is forbidden. He learns this from the פסוק about the firstborn she will bear, which leaves out a woman who cannot give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: The rival wife of an אילונית is forbidden, as it says: "And the firstborn that she bears". This leaves out an אילונית, who does not give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב אסי gives a rule that the צרה of an אילונית is forbidden and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יבום speaks of a woman who can bear a child, so an אילונית is not part of יבום at all. She stays forbidden as an ordinary brother's wife (אשת אח). Because she is forbidden, her צרה is also exempt and may not do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose body never developed so that she can have children
Rival wife: another wife of the same husband
To exclude / this leaves out
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Forbidden here means forbidden to do יבום with the יבם. It does not mean forbidden to marry anyone at all.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
The rival wife of an aylonit is forbidden,
as it is stated:
"And it shall be, the firstborn that she bears"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:6

phrases.english: to exclude an aylonit,
who does not give birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about another kind of forbidden צרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אילונית is left out of יבום by the פסוק, so she stays forbidden as a brother's wife, and her צרה is forbidden too.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a משנה about three brothers and two levirate bonds
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins a challenge to רב אסי. He quotes a משנה: if one brother died, a second brother did מאמר with the widow, and then he died too, both women do חליצה and not יבום, because she is tied to two יבמין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: Three brothers were married to three unrelated women. One of them died, and the second brother did מאמר with the widow, and then he died. These women do חליצה and do not do יבום, as it says: "And one of them dies... her יבם shall come upon her". This means a woman tied to one יבם, and not a woman tied to two יבמין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת opens a challenge against רב אסי by quoting a משנה. This step only lays out the משנה; the actual point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, the first widow is tied to two dead brothers at once, so neither she nor the second brother's wife may do יבום; both do חליצה. The challenge to רב אסי does not come from this ruling itself. It comes from רב יוסף's comment on this משנה (next step), whose words 'this is' will be read as saying that only this case makes a צרה forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
A levirate betrothal, a kind of קידושין the חכמים set up before יבום
They do חליצה, the ceremony that frees a widow from יבום
They do יבום, marrying the יבם
The bond that ties a widow to her יבם

steps.confusionAlert: נכריות here does not mean non-Jewish women. It only means the three wives are not related to each other or to the brothers.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
Three brothers
are married to three unrelated women,
and one of them died,
and the second brother performed levirate betrothal with her,
and he died —
these women perform ḥalitza
and do not enter into levirate marriage,
phrases.notes: "These" means the first brother's widow and the second brother's own wife.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"And one of them dies
her brother-in-law shall come upon her" —
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: one who has upon her the bond of one yavam,
and not the bond of two yevamin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב אסי's rule from step 19 by quoting a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that the צרה of an אילונית is forbidden because a פסוק leaves the אילונית out of יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is setup only. The משנה is the base for רב יוסף's comment (step 21), and in step 22 רב ששת reads its 'this is' as excluding every other case, so the צרת אילונית would be permitted.

steps.title: רב יוסף's comment on the משנה about two יבמין
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת continues his challenge by quoting רב יוסף's comment on the משנה. He calls this the one case in the whole Torah where a woman's falling to the יבם made her צרה forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on that משנה it was taught: רב יוסף said, this is the case of the צרה of a paternal brother's wife, where only the falling to the יבם caused her to be forbidden. We do not find anything like this anywhere else in the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is still building his challenge. Here he quotes רב יוסף's comment on the משנה from step 20, and in the next step he will use its wording to attack רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשת אח מאב is a normal, fully fit יבמה, so nothing about her own status makes her forbidden. The only reason her צרה becomes forbidden is that she fell before the יבם, and רב יוסף says this situation is one of a kind.

keyTerms.meaning: The co-wife of a brother's wife, where the brothers share a father. This is a normal case of יבום.
The prohibition that comes from 'falling', meaning the moment she became tied to the יבם
"And it was taught about it": a comment attached to a source

phrases.english: And it is taught about it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה רב ששת just quoted in step 20, about the two brothers and the מאמר.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא צָרַת אֵשֶׁת אָח מֵאָב,
phrases.english: This is the rival wife of a paternal brother's wife,
for whom the prohibition of falling caused it.
phrases.notes: In other words, she became forbidden only because she fell before the יבם, not because of who she is.

phrases.english: For we have not found in the entire Torah
a case like this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source that רב ששת began quoting in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that the צרת אילונית is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup: רב יוסף says this case is unique. The attack itself comes in the next step.

steps.title: Does 'this is' leave out the צרה of an אילונית?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת reads the words 'this is' as leaving out the צרת אילונית, which would mean she is permitted. That goes against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: "This is": what is it meant to leave out? Isn't it meant to leave out the צרה of an אילונית, which would mean she is permitted?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now attacks. He says רב יוסף's word 'this' implies that other cases, like the צרת אילונית, are not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case in the משנה is the only place where a צרה becomes forbidden, then the צרה of an אילונית must be permitted. That directly contradicts רב אסי in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: "To leave out what?": asking what a word is meant to exclude
The co-wife of a woman who cannot have children
She is permitted

phrases.english: "This is": to exclude what?
Is it not to exclude the rival wife of an aylonit, that she is permitted?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wording of רב יוסף's comment from step 21 to attack רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי: the צרת אילונית is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'This is' sounds exclusive: only this case makes a צרה forbidden, so the צרת אילונית would be permitted.

steps.title: 'This is' excludes the צרת אילונית for being even more forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'this is' does exclude the צרת אילונית, but because her rule is stricter. The צרה in the משנה needs חליצה, while the צרת אילונית needs no חליצה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it excludes the צרה of an אילונית, who is forbidden. What does 'this is' mean? This is the case where falling to the יבם caused the prohibition, so her צרה needs חליצה. But the צרה of an אילונית does not even need חליצה. Why? One is from the Torah, and the other is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. It reads רב יוסף's 'this is' as pointing to a milder rule in his case, not as permitting the צרת אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's case is unique because the צרה is forbidden yet still needs חליצה. The צרת אילונית is fully free from both יבום and חליצה, because the Torah itself excludes the אילונית from יבום. The case in the משנה is forbidden only by the חכמים, so it is weaker and still needs חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: That she is forbidden
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from the יבם
From Torah law
From rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: "To exclude" does not have to mean "to permit." Here it means the צרת אילונית falls outside רב יוסף's case because she is even more exempt: no יבום and no חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between a Torah-level exemption, which needs no חליצה at all, and a rabbinic prohibition, which still needs חליצה.

phrases.english: No, it is to exclude the rival wife of an aylonit, that she is forbidden.
And what is "this is"?

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא, דְּאִיסּוּר נְפִילָה גָּרַם לָהּ —
phrases.english: This is the one for whom the prohibition of falling caused it:
her rival wife requires chalitza,
but with an aylonit, the rival wife does not even require chalitza.
What is the reason?
This one is by Torah law, that one is by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: The אילונית's exemption is from the Torah. The case with the מאמר is only rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's reading in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source's wording: 'this is' excludes in the stricter direction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'This is' means only this case forbids the צרה, so the צרת אילונית is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'This is' means only here does the forbidden צרה still need חליצה. The צרת אילונית is fully exempt by Torah law.

steps.title: Challenge from the opening משנה: צרות of an אילונית are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה listing women whose צרות are permitted, including when the woman turns out to be an אילונית. This seems to go against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: and all of them, if they died, refused, were divorced, or were found to be אילונית, their צרות are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב אסי from the opening משנה of the מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if one of the forbidden relatives turns out to be an אילונית, her צרה is permitted to the יבם. But רב אסי said the צרת אילונית is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learned": quoting a משנה
They refused: a girl married off as a minor leaving her husband through מיאון
Their co-wives are permitted

phrases.english: We learned:
And all of them, if they died or refused,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the list of forbidden relatives in the first משנה of יבמות.

phrases.english: or were divorced, or were found to be an aylonit,
their rival wives are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְכוּלָּן אִם מֵתוּ אוֹ מֵיאֲנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering רב ששת, the גמרא brings a different source against רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי: the צרת אילונית is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly permits the צרה of a woman found to be an אילונית.

steps.title: Answer begins: רב אסי's case is when the husband knew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer: there is no contradiction, because רב אסי is talking about a husband who knew she was an אילונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here, it is where he knew about her...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to split the two cases. Here it gives only the first half: רב אסי's ruling applies when the husband knew about her condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband knew she was an אילונית and married her anyway, the marriage is fully valid. She simply cannot have יבום, so her צרה is exempt too, as רב אסי said. The other half, explaining the משנה's case, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is not difficult": the two sources do not really conflict
That he knew about her, meaning he knew she was an אילונית

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where he knew about her,
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי's case: the husband knew she was an אילונית before marrying her. The other half of the answer comes next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge from the משנה in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the husband knew versus did not know.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רב אסי are talking about the same case and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אסי is talking about a husband who knew she was an אילונית. The משנה's case will be explained in the next step.

steps.title: The משנה is about a husband who did not know
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the משנה that permits the צרת אילונית is talking about a husband who did not know she was an אילונית when he married her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, in the משנה, it is a case where he did not know about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it began in step 25. רב אסי speaks about a husband who knew, and the משנה speaks about a husband who did not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband did not know she was an אילונית, the marriage was a mistake and does not count. So she was never truly his wife, and her צרה is permitted. If he knew and married her anyway, the marriage is real, and רב אסי says her צרה is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Here. Points to the case in the משנה.
He knew about her, meaning he was aware she was an אילונית.
A woman who cannot have children because of a physical condition.

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve the same kind of woman. The only difference is whether the husband knew at the time of marriage, and that decides whether the marriage counts at all.

phrases.english: Here, it is where he did not know about her.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the משנה. "Did not know" means he did not know she was an אילונית when he married her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part answer begun in step 25 (כאן... כאן).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: knew vs. did not know
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to permit every צרת אילונית, against רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה permits her only when the husband did not know, because the marriage was a mistake. רב אסי forbids her when he knew.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה says the women 'were found to be' אילוניות, not 'were' אילוניות. This shows the husband discovered it only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact: it says 'were found to be' and not 'were.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with proof from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Were found to be' means something discovered after the fact, so the husband did not know at the wedding. If the משנה meant any אילונית, even one he knew about, it would have said simply 'were.' This confirms the משנה is about the case of not knowing, so it does not contradict רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact. The גמרא is about to bring support from the text itself.
Were found to be. Something discovered later.
Were. Simply describes what they were, known or not.
Learn from this. Closes a proof.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי and the משנה do not argue. Knew she was an אילונית: real marriage, צרה forbidden. Did not know: mistaken marriage, צרה permitted. The word 'were found' in the משנה proves it.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
phrases.notes: This means the משנה's own wording fits the answer just given.

phrases.english: for it teaches 'were found to be,'
and it does not teach 'were.'
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of steps 25-26 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה speaks of a husband who did not know she was an אילונית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's word 'שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ' (were found to be) instead of 'שֶׁהָיוּ' (were).

steps.title: רבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a new statement, which continues after this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It introduces רבא, whose actual statement comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words are here, so nothing has been said yet. The next part will give רבא's words.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא said. Introduces a statement by the אמורא רבא.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the question on רב אסי is settled, a new statement begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the opening words appear here.
